review_notes: Read the whole target file and the GL coordinate ring simp lemmas (matrix_apply, matrix_det) plus downstream uses (SpecialLinearKernel, SpecialLinear, GeneralSpecialLinearSmooth, and a test file). I did not run Lean, so the claims about simp's behaviour come from reading the simp attributes and rewrite order. They are not experimental observations. I considered other identities (for example the comp_quotient lemmas) and did not report them, since they are not clearly good simp lemmas.

findings.excerpt:
theorem quotient_det :
    quotient K n (matrix K n).det = 1 := by
findings.problem: The sibling `quotient_detInverse` and `polynomialToCoordinateRing_det` are `@[simp]`, but `quotient_det` is not. Tagging it as written would not help, because `GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.matrix_det` is a simp lemma that rewrites `(matrix K n).det` to `algebraMap _ _ (determinant K n)`. Simp rewrites the argument first, so the LHS `quotient K n (matrix K n).det` would never match. As a result, `simp` cannot reduce `quotient K n (matrix K n).det` or `quotient K n (algebraMap _ _ (determinant K n))` to 1. Every downstream use calls `rw [..., quotient_det]` or `exact quotient_det K n` by hand, and the proof of `polynomialToCoordinateRing_det` has to undo `matrix_det` with `rw [← matrix_det, quotient_det]`. The two determinant forms are two spellings of one fact, and the simp set covers neither.
findings.proposed_change: Add a simp lemma stated on the simp-normal form, for example `@[simp] theorem quotient_algebraMap_determinant : quotient K n (algebraMap (PolynomialRing K n) (GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K n) (determinant K n)) = 1 := by rw [← matrix_det]; exact quotient_det K n`. Keep `quotient_det` as the non-simp `matrix` form, or add a comment that `matrix_det` blocks it. Optionally also tag `polynomialQuotient_det` (line 145) with `@[simp]` for consistency with `polynomialToCoordinateRing_det`.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then discharge determinant-one goals in the quotient, such as those in SpecialLinearKernel and SpecialLinear. `polynomialToCoordinateRing_det` and similar proofs no longer need manual `rw [← matrix_det]` to undo another simp lemma. The simp set becomes consistent with `quotient_detInverse`.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem matrix_det :
    (matrix K n).det = algebraMap (PolynomialRing K n) (CoordinateRing K n)
      (determinant K n)

findings.excerpt: def entry (i j : n) : CoordinateRing K n := quotient K n (matrix K n i j)
findings.problem: `entry` is an opaque `def` for `quotient K n (matrix K n i j)`, and there is no simp or normalizing lemma that connects the two. The only link is `polynomialEquiv_variable`, which is not simp and is proved with `change`. `matrix_apply` is `@[simp]` and rewrites `matrix K n i j` to `algebraMap _ _ (MvPolynomial.X (i, j))`, so `simp` turns `quotient K n (matrix K n i j)` into `quotient K n (algebraMap _ _ (X (i,j)))`. That is neither `entry K n i j` nor anything with a lemma. There are two competing normal forms for the same element, and no rule picks one. The tests state facts about `entry` and need the manual `simpa only [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.id_apply]` plus `congrArg` machinery.
findings.proposed_change: Choose `entry` as the canonical form. Add `theorem quotient_matrix_apply (i j : n) : quotient K n (matrix K n i j) = entry K n i j := rfl` (not simp, so it cannot be blocked by `matrix_apply`), together with a simp lemma on the post-`matrix_apply` form, `@[simp] theorem quotient_algebraMap_X (i j : n) : quotient K n (algebraMap (PolynomialRing K n) (GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K n) (MvPolynomial.X (i, j))) = entry K n i j := rfl`. Tag `polynomialEquiv_variable` `@[simp]`, or restate it with `mkₐ` and `X`, so that the polynomial-side variables also normalize to `entry`.
findings.benefit: Expressions such as `f (quotient K n (matrix K n i j))` or `polynomialEquiv K n (mkₐ _ (X (i,j)))` then simplify to a single `entry` normal form. Callers no longer have to rely on defeq via `change`, and statements about entries (as in the GeneralSpecialLinearSmooth tests) can be closed by `simp`.
